title: Build live dashboards and animate explainers with Claude
summary: Anthropic introduced Dashboards, which turn plain-language questions into always-current charts connected to BigQuery, Databricks, Snowflake, and Salesforce (beta on paid plans), and Motion, which turns prompts into short animated explainers exportable as MP4 (beta on Team and Enterprise). Docs, Slides, and Design are now out of beta and available on all plans, including Free. Charts show their underlying query and animations are editable code, so results can be checked.

title: Agent observability on the Claude Platform
summary: In public beta, Managed Agents, the Messages API, and the SDKs can send OpenTelemetry traces to any OTel-compatible tool once a destination is added in Claude Console. Each agent turn, model call, and tool use becomes a trace with latency, tokens, and IDs, following OTel GenAI semantic conventions and working with Grafana Cloud, Honeycomb, Datadog, Langfuse, or any OTLP endpoint. This helps debug failures, review agent behavior, build evals from production traces, and track token usage.

title: Claude now works with Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides
summary: Claude for Google Workspace is in public beta as a sidebar add-on for Docs, Sheets, and Slides on all paid plans. It reads the open file and selection and edits directly, defaulting to "Ask before edits" with an optional "Accept all edits" mode, and new beta connectors let it create and edit files from chat while respecting sharing permissions. Enterprise controls such as the Compliance API and customer-managed keys carry over.

title: How Block orchestrates Claude Fable across thousands of pull requests
summary: Block's Bradley Axen describes using Claude Fable 5 to orchestrate large code migrations, with Fable handling high-level design and smaller Opus or Sonnet models doing file edits and tests. The migration spans thousands of PRs, with about a thousand Fable-orchestrated PRs merged, and the approach reportedly cuts cost without hurting quality. Humans keep control of merges and deploys through security checks and two approvals, and Claude refuses to bypass dual approval.

title: Claude Haiku 5.5
summary: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5 (claude-haiku-5-5), billed as its cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model, and about 75% cheaper to run than Haiku 4.5 on average. It is the first Haiku-class model with an adjustable effort setting, and Sonnet 5.5 cache-read prices were halved, which Anthropic says makes most agentic work about 20% cheaper, with Max and Team getting monthly API credit. It targets high-volume work such as classification, summaries, subagents, and live support, while Sonnet and Opus remain better for complex coding.

title: Building effective agent automations
summary: Lance Martin and CJ Avilla published a guide to scheduled agents on Claude Managed Agents (beta), using a "daily-brief" reference implementation that pulls from Slack and GitHub PRs and posts a Slack brief. Setup uses config files for the agent, schedule, memory, vault, and network allowlist applied with `ant apply`, running on Anthropic infrastructure, with credentials kept in a vault outside the sandbox, read-only access, and a per-run spending cap. The patterns, including per-source bookmarks, reporting unreadable sources, and confirming posts before updating the ledger, matter because background agents otherwise fail silently.
